corrected_row: | DOC-A.1-35 | **Correspondence between lowercase and uppercase letters when no locale is in effect**, §15.97 UPPER-CASE / §15.57 LOWER-CASE function, returned-value rule 4 (§15.97.4 r4, §15.57.4 r4), required + need not be documented (VOLUNTARY — kept because the mapping is observable in every program that folds case) | When neither the LOCALE phrase (r2) nor a CHARACTER CLASSIFICATION (r3) is in effect, UPPER-CASE and LOWER-CASE map through the **.NET invariant-culture simple case tables** — `CobolIntrinsics.UpperCase` is `ToUpperInvariant`, `CobolIntrinsics.LowerCase` is `ToLowerInvariant` — identically in every edition and whatever SET LOCALE, `LANG` or `LC_ALL` says. The correspondence is **one character to one character**, so the returned value always has argument-1's length (r5): `a`→`A`, `é`→`É`, `ſ` (U+017F)→`S`, `A`→`a`, `É`→`é`; `ß` stays `ß` (never `SS`), and the Turkish letters dotless `ı` (U+0131) and dotted `İ` (U+0130) have no invariant correspondence and are returned unchanged, as is every other character without one (r6). The Turkish `i`↔`İ` mapping is available only through a locale (the `LOCALE` phrase or a locale classification — DETERMINATION L9, §3, `CobolLocale`). | `conformance:2002/pb64t5_case_locale_phrase` |

corrected_row: | DOC-A.1-51 | **DELETE FILE statement — what deleting the file does**, §14.9.10 DELETE statement, GR20 (§14.9.10.4 GR20), required + documented | A successful DELETE FILE removes **exactly one host file — the connector's resolved path — with one operating-system delete** (`File.Delete`, an unlink on POSIX hosts), for every organization: a sequential, relative or indexed physical file is one host file, and its fixed file attributes live inside it, so no sidecar, index, lock or catalog file exists to be removed (kb/Work PB802). Nothing is moved to a recycle area and nothing can be recovered by the runtime. Before deleting, the file is checked in this order: **open on this connector** → `41` and nothing is deleted (GR13); the GR18 fixed-attribute match, which never fails because the validated attribute set is empty (item 50); **held open by another file connector** — one of this run unit's, or another run unit's (tested by requesting exclusive access to the file: on Windows every outstanding handle refuses it; on Linux and macOS only a handle holding an advisory lock does, which every COBOL.NET file connector's handle holds, so a POSIX unlink never destroys a file another COBOL.NET run unit has open, while a plain open handle of a non-.NET process does not block the delete) → `62` and the file is not deleted (GR15); **absent** → `05`, a successful completion with no action (GR14), and a bare `ASSIGN USING` connector that has never been associated is treated as absent without touching any file; present but not accessible → `37` (GR16); a medium that refuses deletion (a write-protected volume or read-only mount) → `37` (GR17), a sharing refusal raised by the delete itself → `62`, any other host failure → `30`. On success the status is `00` and a later OPEN INPUT of the file reports `35`. Available from COBOL-2023 (COBOLNET0900 below). Implemented in `FileRegistry.DeleteFile` over `HostFile.Probe` and `HostFile.IsHeldByAnother`; the RETRY phrase's handling of the `62` conflict is item 109's. | `conformance:2023/delete_file`; `conformance:2023/delete_file_absent`; `conformance:2023/delete_file_sharing` |

corrected_row: | DOC-A.1-61 | **Dynamic-capacity table — size, location and time of physical allocation**, §8.5.1.9 dynamic-capacity tables (§8.5.1.9.1), required + need not be documented (VOLUNTARY — kept because it explains the cost of growth) | Each `OCCURS DYNAMIC` table is **one managed array of its own, stored outside the record that contains it** (the record holds a reference to it), so growing a table never moves or resizes its containing group. **Time and size:** the array is allocated when the containing data item is created, with room for the larger of the initial current capacity and 4 occurrences — the initial capacity being the FROM integer (or 0), raised to a table VALUE's capacity — and the initial occurrences are initialized at once. It is **reallocated only when a receiving reference or a SET needs a higher capacity than the array holds** (a sending reference beyond the current capacity never allocates or grows the table), by doubling (from at least 4) until it is large enough, never beyond 1,073,741,823 occurrences; newly allocated occurrences, including every intermediate one, are initialized immediately with the element's initial value (whether or not INITIALIZED is written). **Lowering the capacity** (SET … TO / DOWN BY) releases nothing physically — the slots are kept for reuse, as the §8.5.1.9.4 NOTE permits — and an occurrence re-created by a later increase is initialized afresh, never the value it held before. Implemented in `CobolDynTable` (`GrowTo`, `SetCapacity`). ⚠ An allocation the host cannot satisfy is not yet reported as EC-BOUND-TABLE-LIMIT (kb/Work PB1410, open). | — |

corrected_record.notes: VOLUNTARY row (item 61 need not be documented). §8.5.1.9.1 (cite.py --check 8.5.1.9.1 'The size, location, and time of physical allocation of a dynamic-capacity table are implementor-defined' -> OK §8.5.1.9.1 3)). Code read: CobolDynTable ctor allocates new T[Math.Max(open,4)] with open = max(FROM, VALUE capacity) and seeds via GrowTo; GrowTo doubles from >=4 capped at MaxOccurrences and seeds every new slot (i=_count..target) with _seedAt; SetCapacity shrink only lowers _count. Refuter correction: growth is triggered only by a RECEIVING reference (CobolDynTable.RefReceiving) or SET (SetCapacity); RefSending past the capacity returns a scratch slot and never allocates - row said 'a reference'. Re-probe refute-probe/r61.cob at 2023 matches (C0=2, C1=10 E5=ABC, C2=3, C3=12 E10=ABC E3=QQQ); 2002 -> COBOLNET0900. cite.py OK §8.5.1.9.1 3); §8.5.1.9.4 NOTE read.

corrected_row: | DOC-A.1-42 | **Cultural ordering table — allowable content of the literal that identifies it**, §12.3.7 SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, GR17 (§12.3.7.4 GR17 — `ORDER TABLE ordering-name-1 IS literal-9`), conditionally required (the cultural-ordering facility is provided, A.4.9 item 11) + documented | literal-9 (an alphanumeric or national literal, or a concatenation expression of that class, neither zero-length nor a symbolic-character figurative constant — §12.3.7.3 SR10/SR11, COBOLNET0898; ⚠ today every figurative constant, SPACE and ALL literal included, is also refused with COBOLNET0898, which §8.3.3.6.3 SR1 does not permit — an open defect) may name: **(1)** the ISO/IEC 14651:2020 default table **`ISO 14651_2020_TABLE1`**, matched case-insensitively with spaces and underscores interchangeable and any run of them treated as one (`iso_14651_2020_table1` is the same table) — the CLDR root collation (UCA 17.0.0) in its ISO/IEC 14651-style four-level configuration; or **(2)** as an implementor extension, a **locale tag** (`-` or `_` separators) that this implementation knows: one with a CLDR collation file of its own or of its region-less form, one with a site `.tailor` file, or a culture .NET recognizes. A `-u-co-` collation type is honoured (`de-u-co-phonebk` is German phonebook order); a locale with CLDR data takes its tailored order (`sv_SE` orders `ä` after `b`, where the default table puts it before), and a culture .NET recognizes that no collation data covers collates by the root order. Any other spelling — including another edition's table name such as `ISO 14651_2011_TABLE1` — is legal source that draws the **COBOLNET1662 warning**, and every `FUNCTION STANDARD-COMPARE` reference to that ordering-name sets **EC-ORDER-NOT-SUPPORTED** (§15.85.4 r2); with that checking off the function returns `=`. The compile-time advice and the run-time resolution are one resolver, `CollationEngine.TryGetOrderingTable` (bound in `DataBinder.OrderTableBind`). The clause is COBOL-2002 and later; below 2002 it is COBOLNET0900. | `conformance:2002/pb101_standard_compare`; `conformance:2002/pb101_ec_order_not_supported` |
